prompts: Use case: illustration-story. Create an original heritage-style editorial illustration for an Odia proverb: when a forest burns everybody sees it; when the heart burns nobody knows. Wide landscape, two balanced narrative vignettes on warm handmade ivory paper, inspired by Odisha Pattachitra flat storytelling, fine dark ink contours, muted mineral red, ochre, indigo and leaf green, restrained floral border. Left distant forest with stylized small flames and visible smoke, two villagers notice from safe distance. Right one ordinary adult seated quietly at a veranda, hand resting over chest, composed face with subtle sadness, surrounding space calm. No literal burning human or flaming heart, no injury, no spectacle. Explain visible calamity versus inward grief visually. Simple culturally credible draped everyday clothing, no royal or religious identifiers. Original contemporary interpretation, not simulated antique or archival artefact. No words, letters, logos or watermarks. Hand-painted irregularities, gentle paper texture, generous breathing space.

Use case: illustration-story. Original heritage-style explanatory still life for an Odia saying about an impressive betel pouch that contains neither betel leaves nor areca nuts: outward show without substance. Wide landscape illustration on warm ivory handmade paper, inspired by Odisha Pattachitra fine black contours and flat muted ochre, vermilion, indigo and leaf-green pigments, modest floral border. Show ONE beautifully decorated traditional cloth drawstring betel pouch fully opened towards viewer, its visible inner lining completely empty, wide mouth and cloth folds anatomically plausible. Decorative tassels suggest outward grandeur. Beside it, small separate subdued comparison vignette of two green heart-shaped betel leaves and two small brown areca nuts on a plain brass saucer, clearly outside the pouch. Main empty pouch occupies two thirds, comparison much smaller. No people, tobacco, text, arrows, logos, watermarks. Handmade irregular lines, editorial clarity, original modern interpretation not archival art.

Use case: illustration-story. Original heritage-style editorial illustration for Odia proverb: Is khaja an extraordinary treat for a king's son? Explain how something special can become ordinary with easy access. Wide landscape warm handmade ivory paper, Odisha Pattachitra-inspired flat narrative painting, restrained floral border, fine dark contours, muted mineral vermilion ochre indigo and leaf green. A modestly dressed attendant offers a small brass plate of Odisha khaja: several golden rectangular layered flaky folded pastry pieces, not round ladoos or jalebi. A relaxed young adult prince seated simply in a palace veranda looks mildly unsurprised, gently acknowledging the offering, no contempt. In background on a low serving table sits another small plate of the SAME rectangular layered khaja, conveying familiar ready access, not excessive banquet. Credible elegant draped clothes and subtle head ornament, no deity, no recognizable historical ruler or specific dynasty. No text, logo, watermark or fake antiquing. Gentle expressive human faces, well-formed hands, calm composition. Original interpretive art.
